finish_summary: Simplified priority32 by removing a redundant final mux term in the idx_0 priority-encoder chain (the original `a_i[0] ? 5'd0 : 5'd0` always evaluates to 5'd0 regardless of a_i[0], and separately replaced the outer `hit_0 ? {1,idx_0} : 6'd0` mux with a direct concatenation `{hit_0, idx_0}`, which is equivalent since idx_0 is already 0 whenever hit_0 is 0). This is proven cycle-exact equivalent via Yosys equiv_induct and passes the full simulation benchmark. I explored several alternative codings (balanced binary leading-one-detector tree, one-hot casez priority decoder, explicit shared OR-reduction tree for the hit flag) via estimate_ppa; all converged to the same or worse post-synthesis area/timing than the simplified cascaded-mux version, confirming that ABC's logic optimization already finds the same minimal netlist regardless of RTL structural style for this function, so no further RTL-level restructuring was fruitful. The simplified design was verified end-to-end with place_and_route: area 201.096 um^2, WNS 7.66747 ns, score 76.473604 (baseline was 208.81 um^2, WNS 7.64557 ns, score 76.24689), an improvement of about +0.227 in score through area and slack gains. This is the best verified result and is submitted as final.
